template: A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. A second quantity is determined from x using the factor {factor}. What is the base-{base} logarithmic value associated with this new quantity?
A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. A second quantity is determined from x using the divisor {divisor}. What is the base-{base} logarithmic value associated with this new quantity?
A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. A second quantity is determined from x using the exponent {power}. What is the base-{base} logarithmic value associated with this new quantity?
A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. How is x represented on the natural-logarithm scale?
A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. For the function f(t)=ln(t), what is the rate of change at the value determined by x?
A sound has intensity {intensity} and reference intensity {reference}. What is the resulting level on a base-{base} logarithmic scale?
A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. At x={value}, what is the base-{base} logarithmic representation of the proportion associated with observations up to that point?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. At x={value}, what is the base-{base} logarithmic representation of the proportion of outcomes from the beginning of the interval up to that point?
A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. A cutoff is determined from its spread using the parameter {scale}. What proportion of the distribution lies below this cutoff?
A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. A location on its support is determined from its spread and the parameter {scale}. What is the accumulated proportion at that location?
Two positive quantities {x} and {y}, together with the parameters {power} and {divisor}, determine a final quantity. What is the base-{base} logarithmic representation of that quantity?

For positive quantities {x} and {y}, a new quantity is determined using their ratio and the exponent {power}. What is the natural-logarithm value associated with its base-{base} logarithmic representation?
A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. A new exponent is determined from x using {power}. What positive quantity corresponds to that exponent on the base-{base} scale?
Two positive quantities x and y satisfy {base}^x = {value} and log base {base}(y) = x. For f(t)=ln(t), what is the rate of change at the value y?
A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. At x={value}, the distribution determines a positive level p. What is the rate of change of the natural logarithm at the value ln(p)?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}] and is transformed to Y={multiplier}X+{shift}. Relative to a reference center {reference_mean} and reference spread {reference_sd}, where is the mean of Y located?

A study records {count} events among {total} observations. A future sample contains {sample_size} observations and uses critical value {z}. What uncertainty range should be associated with the estimated proportion?

A population has a characteristic proportion of {p}/100. A sample of {sample_size} observations is used with critical value {z}. Relative to the original proportion, where is the lower end of the resulting estimate located on the standard-error scale?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}] and undergoes the transformations Y={a}X+{b} and Z={c}Y+{d}. Relative to {reference_mean}, how is the mean of Z positioned when {reference_sd} is used as the reference spread?

A pilot study records {count} events among {total} observations. A future study uses {sample_size} observations with critical value {z}. What uncertainty should be reported for the updated planning proportion obtained from the available study information?

A pilot study records {count} events among {total} observations. A future sample contains {sample_size} observations and uses critical value {z}. How far is the lower end of the resulting estimate from the pilot proportion on the standard-error scale?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. At x={value}, a proportion is determined and then modified using {power} and {factor}. What is the base-{base} logarithmic representation of the resulting quantity?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. Consider the portion of the support ending at {value}. A quantity is determined from this portion using {factor} and {divisor}. What is its base-{base} logarithmic value?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. Its distribution determines a population proportion for a sample of {sample_size}, with critical value {z}. What margin of uncertainty should be assigned to the estimated proportion?

A sound has intensity {intensity} and reference intensity {reference}. The resulting level is adjusted using {factor} and {divisor}. What is the final representation on a base-{base} logarithmic scale?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}] and passes through three successive linear calibration stages with parameters ({a},{b}), ({c},{d}), and ({e},{f}). Relative to {reference_mean}, where is the final mean located when {reference_sd} is used as the reference spread?

A population has a characteristic proportion of {p}/100. A sample of {sample_size} observations is considered with critical value 1. What is the final standardized uncertainty when the planning proportion is determined from the initial estimate and an adjustment factor of 2?

A quantity x satisfies {base}^x = {value}. A new exponent is determined from x using the factors {factor} and {factor2}. What positive quantity corresponds to that exponent on the base-{base} exponential scale?

A pilot study records {count} events among {total} observations. A future sample contains {sample_size} observations and uses critical value 1. What is the final standardized uncertainty based on the information from the pilot study?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}] and undergoes three successive linear transformations with parameters ({m1},{s1}), ({m2},{s2}), and ({m3},{s3}). A reference system is specified by {reference_mean} and {reference_sd}. What are the mean and standard deviation at the final stage?

A survey records {count} positive outcomes among {total} observations. A future sample contains {sample_size} observations and uses critical value {z}. What is the final standardized uncertainty based on the original survey proportion?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}]. Its distribution determines a population proportion used with a sample of {sample_size} and critical value {z}. What margin of uncertainty results after the estimated proportion is updated from the initial estimate?

A random variable X is uniformly distributed on [0, {support}] and passes through five successive linear calibration stages with parameter pairs ({m1},{s1}), ({m2},{s2}), ({m3},{s3}), ({m4},{s4}), and ({m5},{s5}). What are the mean and standard deviation at the final stage?

A study records {count} events among {total} observations. A future study uses {sample_size} observations with critical value 1. What final value describes the uncertainty on the reference scale based on the initial study and the future sampling plan?
